question: On a CT scan, how does dense bone usually appear?
explanation: Bone absorbs a lot of radiation, so it shows up as a bright white color on the image. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a CT scan and a regular X-ray?

options.A: It requires no computer processing at all
options.B: It uses sound waves instead of radiation
options.C: It only images the superficial skin layers

explanation: While both use X-rays, a regular X-ray gives a flat, 2D shadow, but a CT scan gives detailed cross-sectional slices like slicing a loaf of bread. Great job! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why might a patient be given oral contrast before a CT scan?

options.A: To numb the lining of the throat for comfort
options.B: To outline the stomach and intestines clearly
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure during the test
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions to intravenous dye

explanation: Swallowing oral contrast helps coat the gut so doctors can easily spot issues like blockages. Simple and smart! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which lab test is most important to check before giving a patient intravenous contrast?
explanation: Serum creatinine tells us how well the kidneys are working. Since contrast leaves through the kidneys, we need to make sure they can handle it safely. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h2)

question: Why must patients take off all jewelry and metal objects before a CT scan?

options.A: Metal attracts the magnetic radiation from the machine
options.B: Metal heats up dangerously during the scan process
options.C: Metal objects cause artifact streaks on the images
options.D: Metal interferes with the hospital Wi-Fi signals

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely and creates ugly, bright streaks on the scan that can hide important details. Always good to remember in clinicals! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h3)

question: A patient is scheduled for an abdominal CT with IV contrast. What is the very first thing a nurse should check?

options.A: Administer a full dose of oral laxatives to clear the bowel
options.B: Assess the patient for a history of seafood or iodine allergies
options.C: Shave the hair on the patient's abdomen near the umbilicus
options.D: Insert an indwelling urinary catheter for continuous output

explanation: Safety first! Checking for allergies prevents severe reactions to the iodine contrast. You are thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is a normal, harmless feeling a patient might report right after getting an IV contrast injection?

options.A: Severe sharp pain in the chest
options.B: Sudden numbness in both lower legs
options.C: A warm flushing feeling and metallic taste
options.D: An intense urge to vomit continuously

explanation: It's totally normal for patients to feel a sudden warm rush and taste metal in their mouth. Warn your patients beforehand so they don't panic! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why is it super important for a patient to stay completely still during a CT scan?

options.A: Motion blurs the images and requires a repeat scan
options.B: Moving triggers an emergency shutdown of the scanner
options.C: Movement can cause the motorized table to break
options.D: Patient movement stops the release of contrast dye

explanation: Movement messes up the computer's picture, making the scan blurry and useless. Staying still helps get it right the first time! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients to drink plenty of fluids after a CT scan with contrast?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry after fasting
options.B: To help flush the contrast dye out through the kidneys
options.C: To replace electrolytes lost during the scanning process
options.D: To keep the intravenous catheter from clotting shut

explanation: Pushing fluids helps the kidneys wash out the contrast quickly and safely. Hydration is key! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing check after a contrast CT scan?

options.A: Evaluating baseline lung sounds for sudden fluid overload
options.B: Checking the intravenous site for swelling or leakage
options.C: Monitoring the patient for delayed allergic rashes
options.D: Encouraging the patient to drink plenty of fluids

explanation: Unless there's a specific heart or kidney issue, checking lung sounds isn't part of routine post-CT care. But checking the IV site, watching for rashes, and pushing fluids definitely are! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h5)
